item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: Severe flooding has struck the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa district, roughly a year after massive floods caused widespread destruction in the region near the Nepal-China border.

Local officials confirmed that the flood originated across the border in Tibet.

Citing dangerously high water levels, the District Administration Office, Rasuwa, has urged residents along the riverbanks in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha, and Chitwan districts to evacuate to safer locations.

At 9:30 a.m. on Wednesday, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) issued an urgent notice warning of an elevated risk of severe flooding in the Trishuli River.

The Bhotekoshi merges with the Ghattekhola River, which originates from the sacred Gosainkunda Lake just above Dhunche, to form the Trishuli River. The Trishuli is a major tributary of the Narayani River. It is known as the Gandak after entering India and is one of the major tributaries of the Ganges.

In July of last year, similar flooding in the Lhende River washed away a key bridge linking Nepal and China and destroyed multiple sections of the essential Dhunche–Rasuwagadhi highway. Satellite data analyzed by organizations like ICIMOD confirmed that a glacial lake on the Purugu Glacier north of Langtang Himal rapidly expanded and ruptured. This sent a violent torrent of water downstream into the Lhende River catchment areas.

item.title: RPP expels three lawmakers for joining Bagmati government
item.dc:creator: bishnu

RPP Chairperson Rajendra Lingden said the party had removed Bagmati provincial lawmakers Raju Bista, Rajendra Prajapati and Gir Bahadur Tamang from their positions. He said the lawmakers were removed for repeatedly defying […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: Three provincial lawmakers from the Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP) in Bagmati Province have been relieved of their positions for violating party directives.

RPP Chairperson Rajendra Lingden said the party had removed Bagmati provincial lawmakers Raju Bista, Rajendra Prajapati and Gir Bahadur Tamang from their positions.

He said the lawmakers were removed for repeatedly defying party directives, violating the party whip and joining the provincial government against the decision of the party’s Central Committee.

“Since the RPP Central Work Execution Committee has decided to remove the three as provincial assembly members and declare their positions vacant basedon the recommendation of the Disciplinary Committee, as they were involved in supporting the government or joining the government in contrary to the decisions and directives of the party, in violation of Article 30(d) of the RPP Statute, I request that their positions be declared vacant,” Lingden said in the letter addressed to Speaker of Bagmati Province.

Earlier, the party had removed its parliamentary party leader in Bagmati, Uddhav Thapa, from office after he defied party orders by extending RPP’s support to CPN-UML’s Kiran Thapa to form the provincial government.

Meanwhile, the Patan High Court has declined to issue a stay order against the appointment of Kiran Thapa as Bagmati Chief Minister.

However, the high court’s Hetauda bench issued a show-cause notice directing the defendants to explain why a stay order should not be granted as requested by the petitioners.

A single bench of High Court Judge Babita Upreti issued the order, directing the defendants to submit a written response within 15 days, according to Deputy Registrar Badri Prasad Lamichhane.

Two separate petitions have been lodged at the high court, challenging the appointment of Thapa as the chief minister.

The meeting of the Bagmati Province Assembly, originally called for 1 p.m. on Monday for the purpose of taking a vote of confidence, was rescheduled for 5 pm. After the meeting failed to convene at the scheduled time, it was rescheduled for 8 p.m.  However, the meeting did not convene at the scheduled time.

The meeting has now been rescheduled for 4:00 p.m. on Tuesday.

item.title: NC issues whip to vote against Bagmati Chief Minister Thapa
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: The Nepali Congress (NC) parliamentary party in the Bagmati Provincial Assembly has issued a whip directing its lawmakers to vote against the motion of confidence of Chief Minister Kiran Thapa. Chief Minister Thapa is scheduled to take a vote of confidence in the provincial assembly on Monday. In the whip issued by Pukar Maharjan, […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: The Nepali Congress (NC) parliamentary party in the Bagmati Provincial Assembly has issued a whip directing its lawmakers to vote against the motion of confidence of Chief Minister Kiran Thapa.

Chief Minister Thapa is scheduled to take a vote of confidence in the provincial assembly on Monday.

In the whip issued by Pukar Maharjan, chief whip of the NC parliamentary party in the Bagmati Provincial Assembly, lawmakers have been directed to be present at the provincial assembly meeting and vote against the motion of confidence tabled by Chief Minister Thapa.

The NC issued the whip in accordance with Article 168 (4) of the Constitution of Nepal, 2015, and Rule 143 of the Bagmati Provincial Assembly Rules, 2017.

Thapa, who represents CPN-UML, was sworn in as Chief Minister of Bagmati on Thursday. He leads a coalition government of the UML, the Nepali Communist Party (NCP) and the Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP).

UML formed the new coalition after the NC announced its exit from the NC-UML coalition in provincial governments. UML subsequently withdrew its support from the Indra Bahadur Baniya-led provincial government in Bagmati.

After losing the majority in the provincial assembly, Baniya tendered his resignation on August 17.

item.dc:creator: bishnu

item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: Police have arrested three suspects for the murder of 22-year-old Basanta Kalathoki in a hostel in Shankhamul of Kathmandu on Friday morning.

According to District Police Range, Kathmandu, Kalathoki, who was severely injured following an attack with a sharp weapon, died while undergoing treatment at Civil Hospital, Kathmandu, at around 12 noon of the same day.

Police have taken 19-year-old Shekhar Yadav of Kalaiya Sub-Metropolitan City-3, Bara, who was also staying at the hostel, into custody in connection with the incident. Another 19-year-old suspect, Pramit Patel, who was also staying at the hostel, was arrested in Bhainse with the help of the District Police Office, Makwanpur.

Police have also arrested the owner of the hostel, 23-year-old Alok Thakur of Loharpatti Municipality-6, Mahottari.

The Kathmandu District Court has granted police permission to keep the suspects in custody for five days for further investigation, according to the District Police Range, Kathmandu.

item.title: Dispute erupts in RPP after Bagmati leader backs UML
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: Disputes have erupted within the Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP) over supporting the alliance of CPN-UML and the Nepali Communist Party (NCP) to form a government in Bagmati Province. RPP has decided to take action against its parliamentary party leader in Bagmati, Uddhab Thapa, after he defied the party’s instruction and decided to support Kiran […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: Disputes have erupted within the Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP) over supporting the alliance of CPN-UML and the Nepali Communist Party (NCP) to form a government in Bagmati Province.

RPP has decided to take action against its parliamentary party leader in Bagmati, Uddhab Thapa, after he defied the party’s instruction and decided to support Kiran Thapa Magar of UML to form a government in the province.

RPP Chairperson Rajendra Lingden has already sought an explanation from him over his decision.

RPP’s support is crucial for the UML-NCP alliance, which together has 55 seats in the 110-member provincial assembly. A majority of 56 is needed to form a government in the province. RPP has 13 seats in the province, including the Speaker.

Meanwhile, RPP’s Chief Whip in the Bagmati Province Assembly Kumari Tamang has urged Province Chief Deepak Raj Bhatta not to recognize the support submitted by Thapa.

In a letter sent to Province Chief Bhatta on Wednesday, Tamang said Thapa had submitted the letter of support on his personal letterhead without convening a meeting of the provincial parliamentary party.

“We were surprised to learn through the media that RPP Bagmati Province parliamentary party leader Uddhav Thapa, without convening a meeting of the parliamentary party, arbitrarily supported CPN-UML Bagmati Province Assembly member Kiran Thapa Magar for chief minister and submitted a letter to the Province Chief using his personal letterhead,” she said in the letter.

The RPP is scheduled to hold a central committee meeting on Thursday, where the dispute over the Bagmati Province parliamentary party’s decision is expected to be discussed.

item.title: Bagmati Chief Minister Baniya announces resignation
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: Bagmati Province Chief Minister Indra Bahadur Baniya has announced his resignation. Addressing a meeting of the provincial assembly on Monday, Baniya announced that he would step down from the post. Baniya was scheduled to take a vote of confidence on Monday after his coalition government with the CPN-UML fell into a minority following the […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: Bagmati Province Chief Minister Indra Bahadur Baniya has announced his resignation.

Addressing a meeting of the provincial assembly on Monday, Baniya announced that he would step down from the post.

Baniya was scheduled to take a vote of confidence on Monday after his coalition government with the CPN-UML fell into a minority following the latter’s withdrawal of support. He stepped down after it became certain that he wouldn’t pass the floor test.

UML has already formed a new alliance with the Nepali Communist Party (NCP) to form a new government in the province. As per the understanding between the two parties, UML will form the government in the province with the support of the NCP.

A majority of 53 is needed to form a government in the 104-member Bagmati Provincial Assembly. Baniya had the support of only 36 lawmakers from his party and two from the Hamro Nepal Party (HNP).

Baniya was appointed chief minister of Bagmati Province on August 5, 2025, after he removed Bahadur Singh Tamang as the NC’s parliamentary party leader in the provincial assembly.

Addressing the provincial assembly, Baniya claimed that his government had carried out various works in the interests of the people of the province during his tenure. Although much remained to be done, he said he was compelled to resign due to the changing political circumstances.

item.dc:creator: bishnu

According to the District Police Office, Rasuwa, the identity of the deceased has not been established yet. “Three injured have been airlifted to […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: At least one person was killed and six others, including two Nepali Army personnel, were injured in an explosion at Mangchet in Ama Chhodingmo Rural Municipality-4, Rasuwa, on Monday, police said.

According to the District Police Office, Rasuwa, the identity of the deceased has not been established yet.

“Three injured have been airlifted to Kathmandu for treatment, while the other three are receiving treatment in Rasuwa,” said Inspector Dilli Raj Sapkota, information officer at the District Police Office, Rasuwa.

Sapkota said police were investigating the cause of the explosion. “Our first focus was on rescuing the injured. Now, we will begin an investigation into what caused the explosion,” he added.

Nepali Army Spokesperson Brigadier General Rajaram Basnet said the explosion occurred during the disposal of expired explosives at an army barracks. “The explosives were procured for blasting boulders for several hydropower and road projects in the area,” Basnet said.

“The injured were airlifted to Kathmandu by a Nepal Army rescue flight,” Basnet said.

item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: Police have identified the woman who was killed in a bus crash on the Ring Road in Gwarko of Lalitpur on Thursday morning.

The accident occurred at around 10:15 am when a bus crashed into the retaining wall of the Gwarko flyover in Lalitpur-17. Metropolitan City. The bus reportedly went out of control, hit the wall and overturned, killing one woman.

The deceased has been identified as Jenisha Lama (40) of Dolakha.

Police have taken the driver of the bus, Lakshi Tamang (36), from Timal of Kavre, for necessary investigation.

A total of 18 people were injured in the accident. Nine of the injured are receiving treatment at B & B Hospital, while the remaining nine have been sent to Global Hospital, police say.

item.title: Baniya joins hands with HNP in a bid to save his govt
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: Bagmati Chief Minister Indra Bahadur Baniya has begun efforts to save his government after losing a majority in the provincial assembly following the CPN-UML’s decision to withdraw support. In a bid to strengthen his position, Baniya on Tuesday appointed Hamro Nepal Party (HNP) lawmaker Shailendra Man Bajracharya as the Minister for Physical Infrastructure Development. […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: Bagmati Chief Minister Indra Bahadur Baniya has begun efforts to save his government after losing a majority in the provincial assembly following the CPN-UML’s decision to withdraw support.

In a bid to strengthen his position, Baniya on Tuesday appointed Hamro Nepal Party (HNP) lawmaker Shailendra Man Bajracharya as the Minister for Physical Infrastructure Development.

The appointment, however, is unlikely to be enough to salvage his administration. The HNP holds only two seats in the 110-member provincial assembly, where a majority of 56 votes is needed to form or save the government. Baniya’s party, the Nepali Congress (NC), holds 37 seats in the provincial assembly. Even if NC secures the backing of every party outside the CPN-UML and the Nepali Communist Party (NCP), it would still fall short of the mark. Adding 13 lawmakers from the Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP), three from the Nepal Workers and Peasants Party (NWPP), and two from the HNP brings Baniya’s total to just 55 members—one short of a majority.

Nevertheless, inducting the HNP into the cabinet carries strategic weight as it effectively prevents the CPN-UML and NCP, who together command 55 seats, from securing the HNP’s support to stake their own claim to form the next government. With the HNP now aligned with the ruling coalition, the UML–NCP alliance must win over either the 13-member RPP or the three-member NWPP to take power.

These shifting coalition dynamics have turned the Bagmati Province Assembly into a continuous game of political musical chairs following the hung assembly delivered by the 2022 provincial elections. The province has already seen three chief ministers, reflecting volatile central-level alliances of the NC, UML, and NCP.

Shalikram Jamkattel of the CPN (Maoist Centre), which has now become the NCP following its merger with the CPN (Unified Socialist), formed the first provincial government after the 2022 elections with support from the UML and CPN (Unified Socialist). The coalition held power for about a year and a half.

When a new NC–UML alliance was formed, Bahadur Singh Lama of the NC assumed office as Chief Minister. After roughly a year, Indra Bahadur Baniya took over as Chief Minister under the same NC–UML backing following an intense power struggle within the NC’s parliamentary party.

Now, the UML and NCP have announced a new alliance to form new governments in all seven provinces. As per the understanding between the two parties, the UML is slated to head Bagmati with NCP support. However, the process has hit a roadblock due to internal disputes within the UML over the selection of the chief minister and the HNP’s decision to side with incumbent Chief Minister Baniya.
